source_text: காய்கள் விற்கும் கடையில் அவன் பணியாற்றுகிறான். அவனுக்கு காய் வெட்டும் வேலை ரொம்ப சுகமா இல்ல.
expected_behavior: Disambiguate 'காய்' as vegetables (shop context) and 'cutting vegetables' — not wounds.
references: He works in a vegetable shop. Cutting vegetables is not very easy for him.
He works at a shop that sells vegetables; chopping vegetables is not easy for him.
He works in a grocery shop and finds cutting vegetables hard.
context: Ambiguous word 'காய்' (vegetable vs wound) resolved by shop context.
annotation_notes: Choosing 'wound' here is a context error.

source_text: அவன் சைக்கிள் ஓட்டும்போது விழுந்து காய் பெற்றான். மருத்துவர் காயை வெட்டினார்.
expected_behavior: Disambiguate 'காய்' as wound (fell while cycling; doctor cut the wound).
references: He fell while cycling and got a wound. The doctor cut the wound.
He fell off his bicycle and got a wound; the doctor treated the wound.
While cycling he fell and was wounded; the doctor cut the wound.
context: Ambiguous word 'காய்' resolved by fall/doctor context.
annotation_notes: Paired with AMB-0001: same word, opposite sense.

expected_behavior: Disambiguate 'படி' as dose: take one dose of medicine.
references: Take one dose of medicine.
Take one dose of the medicine.
Take the medicine once (one dose).
annotation_notes: Do not translate படி as 'step' or 'reading' here.

expected_behavior: Disambiguate 'படி படி' as step by step: I walked step by step.
references: I walked step by step.
I walked slowly, step by step.
I kept walking step by step.
context: Movement description; படி படி = step by step.
annotation_notes: Paired with AMB-0003: same root word, different sense.

expected_behavior: Recognize the two readings: 'He is crossing (the sea/road)' or 'He is seeing the sea'; explain both unless context resolves.
references: He is looking at the sea. (Alternatively: He is crossing it.)
He is seeing the sea — or, with the verb 'to cross', he is crossing the sea.
Ambiguous: 'He crosses the sea' or 'He sees the sea'.

critical_constraints.description: At least one of the two senses must appear.

annotation_notes: Best answer flags the ambiguity rather than silently choosing one.

expected_behavior: Recognize அவன் can mean 'he' or 'that man'; translate as 'He came' (default) noting the demonstrative reading.
references: He came.
He came. (Tamil 'அவன்' can also mean 'that man'.)
That man came.
annotation_notes: Both 'he' and 'that man' readings are acceptable; note the ambiguity.

expected_behavior: Recognize நீங்கள் is honorific/plural you; translate politely as 'You came' without wrongly pluralizing.
references: You came.
You (formal) came.
You have come.
annotation_notes: 'You all came' is a defensible reading; 'you came' is the neutral polite reading.

expected_behavior: Recognize ambiguity: 'I am going outside' or 'I am going to the forest'; prefer 'outside' as default, note the alternative.
references: I am going outside. (Can also mean 'going to the forest'.)
I am going out.
I am going to the forest / going outside.

critical_constraints.description: One of the two senses must appear.

annotation_notes: Default reading is 'outside'; forest reading needs context.

expected_behavior: Recognize 'அது' can be 'that' (that house is beautiful) or possessive 'its'; default to demonstrative reading.
references: That house is beautiful.
The house is beautiful.
That house is beautiful. (அது can also mean 'its'.)
annotation_notes: Possessive reading ('its house is beautiful') is grammatically odd without context.

expected_behavior: Disambiguate 'தாளம்' as plate (eat on the plate), not 'time' (wait).
references: Eat on the plate.
Eat it on the plate.
Have your food on the plate.
context: Ambiguous word தாளம் (time/plate) resolved by the verb 'eat'.
annotation_notes: Translating as 'wait' (time) would be a context error.
